questions.q: The resistance of a wire is $5Ω$. Its new resistance in ohm, if stretched to $5$ times of its original length will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The resistance of a wire $( R )$~is related to its resistivity \left(ρ\right)$, length$( l )$~ and~cross-sectional area \left(A\right)$~as:

$R = ρ\dfrac{l}{A}$

As the length of wire increases, the cross-sectional~area decreases. The~cross-sectional~area in terms of volume~$( V )$~and length~$( l )$ is

$A = \dfrac{V}{l}$

$∴ R = ρ\dfrac{l2}{V}$

Taking the volume of wire constant,

$R ∝ l^{2}$

So if~$R^{'}$~is the resistance of wire after getting redrawn and~$R$~is the initial resistance of wire,

$∴ \dfrac{R '}{R} = \dfrac{( 5l{)}^{2}}{l2} = 25 ⇒ R^{'} = 25 \times R = 125Ω$

questions.q: The combination of two identical cells, whether connected in series or parallel combination provides the same current through an external resistance of $2Ω$. The value of internal resistance of each cell is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the cells are connected in series& ${i}_{s} = \dfrac{2ε}{2r + R} = \dfrac{2ε}{2r + 2}$

When they are connected in parallel, the emf is~${ε}_{p} = \dfrac{\dfrac{ε}{r} + \dfrac{ε}{r}}{\dfrac{1}{r} + \dfrac{1}{r}} = ε$~and the effective internal resistance will be~${r}_{p} = \dfrac{r \times r}{r + r} = \dfrac{r}{2}$. Therefore, the current will be,

${i}_{p} = \dfrac{ε}{R + \dfrac{r}{2}} = \dfrac{ε}{2 + \dfrac{r}{2}} = \dfrac{2ε}{4 + r}$

Since,~${i}_{s} = {i}_{p} ⇒ \dfrac{2ε}{2r + 2} = \dfrac{2ε}{4 + r} ⇒ r = 2Ω$

Therefore, $%$ change in power $=$

$\dfrac{{P}_{final} - {P}_{int}}{Pint} \times 100 = \left(0 .64 - 1\right) \times 100 = - 36%$

questions.q: Equivalent resistance between the adjacent corners of a regular $n$-sided polygon of uniform wire of resistance $R$ would be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given the total resistance of the wire is& $R$. If the polygon has~$n$~numbers of side, then the resistance~ \left(r\right)$, as shown in the following figure,~of each side can be written as

$r = \dfrac{R}{n} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Among all the resistances, \left(n - 1\right)$~resistances are connected in series combination, whereas, their equivalent resistance is connected in parallel with the $n^{th}$~resistance.~The equivalent circuit diagram for the above set of resistances can be depicted as follows:

From the above equivalent circuit diagram, the net equivalent resistance~ \left({R}_{eq}\right)$~for the entire combination can be calculated as follows-

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{Req} & = & \dfrac{1}{\left(n - 1\right)r} + \dfrac{1}{r} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{\left(n - 1\right)\dfrac{R}{n}} + \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{R}{n}} \\ & = & \dfrac{n}{\left(n - 1\right)R} + \dfrac{n}{R} \\ & = & \dfrac{n2}{\left(n - 1\right)R} \\ {R}_{eq} & = & \dfrac{\left(n - 1\right)R}{n2}\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: A battery of $3.0\text{V}$ is connected to a resistor dissipating $0.5\text{W}$ of power. If the terminal voltage of the battery is $2.5\text{V}$, the power dissipated within the internal resistance is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Emf of the battery,& $E = 3V$

Potential difference across resister~$R$~is~${V}_{R} = 2 . 5V$

Power dissipation in the resister is~$P = 0 . 5W$

By using Kirchhoff's voltage law is given by,

${V}_{r} + {V}_{R} = E . . . ( 1 )$

${V}_{r}$~is voltage across internal resister.

Using equation (1) and substitute the given values,

$⇒ {V}_{r} + 2 .5 = 3$

$⇒ {V}_{r} = 0 .5$

Now the ratio of potential across~$R$~and~$r$~is given by,

$\dfrac{VR}{Vr} = \dfrac{IR}{Ir} = \dfrac{2 .5}{0 .5} = 5$

$⇒ \dfrac{R}{r} = 5$

Now the power dissipation across the internal resistance is given by

$\dfrac{PR}{Pr} = \dfrac{I^{2}R}{I^{2}r} = \dfrac{R}{r}$

$⇒ \dfrac{PR}{Pr} = 5$

$⇒ {P}_{r} = \dfrac{PR}{5}$

$⇒ {P}_{r} = \dfrac{0 .5}{5} = 0 .1 W$

questions.q: A wire of length $10$ cm and radius $\sqrt{7} \times {10}^{- 4}m$ connected across the right gap of a meter bridge. When a resistance of $4 . 5Ω$ is connected on the left gap by using a resistance box, the balance length is found to be at $60$ cm from the left end. If the resistivity of the wire is $R \times {10}^{- 7}Ωm$, then value of $R$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the null point condition of a Meter Bridge, it follows that,

$\dfrac{4 . 5Ω}{60} = \dfrac{X}{100 - 60} ⇒ X = \dfrac{40}{60} \times 4 . 5Ω = 3Ω$

Also,

$\begin{cases}X & = & \dfrac{ρl}{A} \\ & = & \dfrac{ρl}{\pir^{2}} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

From equation (1), it follows that

$3 = ρ \times \dfrac{0 . 1}{\pi \times \left(\sqrt{7} \times {10}^{- 4}\right)2} ⇒ ρ = \dfrac{3 \times \pi \times \left(\sqrt{7} \times {10}^{- 4}\right)2}{0 . 1} \approx 66 \times {10}^{- 7}Ωm$

Therefore, $R = 66$.

questions.q: A $1m$ long wire is broken into two unequal parts $X$ and $Y$. The $X$ part of the wire is stretched into another wire $W$. Length of $W$ is twice the length of $X$ and the resistance of $W$ is twice that of $Y$. Find the ratio of length of $X$~and$Y$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resistance of a wire is given by& $R = \dfrac{ρL}{A}$, where,~$ρ$~is conductivity,~$L$~is length of wire and~$A$~is cross-sectional area of wire.

For a single wire,~$A$~and~$ρ$~are constant.

Thus, for parts~$X$~and~$Y$, resistance,~$\dfrac{RX}{RY} = \dfrac{lX}{lY}$.

When wire is stretched to double of its length, then resistance becomes four~times, thus,~${R}_{W} = 4{R}_{X} = 2{R}_{Y}$.

Hence, the ratio is~$\dfrac{RX}{RY} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

So, $\dfrac{lX}{lY} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: In the experiment of Ohm's law, a potential difference of $5 . 0V$ is applied across the end of a conductor of length $10 . 0cm$ and diameter of $5 . 00mm .$ The measured current in the conductor is $2 . 00A .$ The maximum permissible percentage error in the resistivity of the conductor is :-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$R = \dfrac{ρℓ}{A} = \dfrac{V}{I}$
$ρ = \dfrac{AV}{Iℓ} = \dfrac{\pid^{2}V}{4Iℓ} \left($A = $\dfrac{\pid^{2}}{4}\right)
$∴ $\dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} = \dfrac{2\Deltad}{d} + \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} + \dfrac{\Delta I}{I} + \dfrac{\Deltaℓ}{ℓ}
\dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} =$2\left(\dfrac{0 . 01}{5 . 00}\right) + \dfrac{0 . 1}{5 . 0} + \dfrac{0 . 01}{2 . 00} + \dfrac{0 . 1}{10 . 0}
\dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} =$0 . 004 + 0 . 02 + 0 . 005 + 0 . 01$
\dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} =$0 . 039$
$%$ error $= $\dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} \times$100 = 0 . 039 $\times$100 = 3 . 90 % .$

questions.q: A cell of emf $90V$ is connected across series combination of two resistors each of $100Ω$~resistance. A voltmeter of resistance $400Ω$ is used to measure the potential difference across each resistor. The reading of the voltmeter will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,& voltmeter is connected in parallel to the element being measured.

The equivalent resistance of the above circuit is& ${R}_{eq} = \left(\dfrac{400 \times 100}{400 + 100}\right) + 100 = 80 + 100 = 180Ω$

Current through the circuit is~$i = \dfrac{90}{180} = \dfrac{1}{2}A$

Reading of the voltmeter is~${V}_{R} = i\left(\dfrac{400 \times 100}{400 + 100}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 80 = 40V$

questions.q: A metal wire of resistance $3Ω$ is elongated to make a uniform wire of double its previous length. This new wire is now bent and the ends joined to make a circle. If two points on this circle make an angle ${60}^{o}$ at the center, the equivalent resistance between these two points will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know, $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A} = \dfrac{ρl^{2}}{Al} = \dfrac{ρl^{2}}{Volume}$
$R ∝ l^{2}$~, if the volume is constant.
$∴$ New resistance $= 4R$

${R}_{1} = \dfrac{4R}{360} \times 300 = \dfrac{10R}{3}$
${R}_{2} = \dfrac{4R}{360} \times 60 = \dfrac{2R}{3}$
$∴$ Equivalent resistance ${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{{R}_{1}{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1} + {R}_{2}}$
$= \dfrac{\dfrac{10R}{3} \times \dfrac{2R}{3}}{\dfrac{10R}{3} + \dfrac{2R}{3}} = \dfrac{5R}{9}$
$= \dfrac{5}{3}Ω$

The given data is~

$I = 2AA = 25 \times {10}^{- 6}m^{2}n = 2 \times {10}^{28}e = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$

Substituting the given values in equation (i)

$2 = 2 \times {10}^{28} \times 25 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 1 .6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times {v}_{d} ⇒ {v}_{d} = \dfrac{2}{2 \times {10}^{28} \times 25 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 1 .6 \times {10}^{- 19}}$

$⇒ {v}_{d} = \dfrac{1}{25 \times 1 .6 \times 1000}ms^{- 1} = 25 \times {10}^{- 6}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A $220V, 50Hz$ AC source is connected to a $25V, 5W$ lamp and an additional resistance $R$ in series (as shown in figure) to run the lamp at its peak brightness, then the value of $R$ (in ohm) will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resistance of the bulb can be calculated as,

$P = \dfrac{V2}{RB} ⇒ {R}_{B} = \dfrac{V2}{P} = \dfrac{252}{5} = 125Ω$

The current through the bulb for peak brightness should be,

$i = \dfrac{25}{125} = \dfrac{1}{5}A$

Now,~${i}_{rms} = \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{220}{{R}_{B} + R}$

$RB + R = 1100$

$R = 1100 - 125 = 975$
